tour.overview:
Founded by Alexander the Great in 331 BC, Alexandria was for almost a thousand years one of the great cities of the world: capital of the Ptolemies and of Cleopatra, home of the Great Library and of the Pharos, the lighthouse counted among the Seven Wonders. Today it is Egypt's second city, a breezy Mediterranean port of cafés, trams and long seafront promenades, with a character quite different from Cairo.

This private day trip leaves Cairo early by the desert highway and spends the day with a licensed Egyptologist in the city's Greco-Roman past and its seaside present. You descend into the catacombs of Kom el-Shoqafa, where Egyptian gods wear Roman armour, stand beneath Pompey's Pillar, walk the walls of the 15th-century Qaitbay Citadel, built with stones from the fallen lighthouse, and visit the striking Bibliotheca Alexandrina. Lunch is fresh fish chosen at the counter in a seafood restaurant by the harbour.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: about 12 hours
• Start and end: your hotel in Cairo or Giza
• Type: private tour with car, driver and licensed Egyptologist guide
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Level: easy; some steep stairs in the catacombs

WHAT YOU SEE
• The Catacombs of Kom el-Shoqafa.
• Pompey's Pillar and the Serapeum site.
• The Qaitbay Citadel and the Eastern Harbour.
• The Bibliotheca Alexandrina.
• The Corniche along the Mediterranean.

WHY THIS WORKS
A private car makes the long drive comfortable and lets you set the pace. Alexandria's sights are spread out, and a driver who knows the city saves a great deal of time.

WHO IT SUITS
Visitors with three or more days in Cairo, return travellers, history lovers and anyone who wants to see a different side of Egypt.

WHO MAY PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
If you have only one or two days in Cairo, prioritise our Giza and Grand Egyptian Museum tours.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
The drive takes about 3 hours each way. Bring a light jacket, as the sea breeze can be cool in winter. Photography in the catacombs may be restricted.

days.name: Alexandria: catacombs, citadel and library
days.description:
What to expect: a private day trip from Cairo to Alexandria with an Egyptologist, from Roman catacombs to the Mediterranean seafront, with tickets and a seafood lunch.

Your guide and driver collect you at about 7:00 and take the desert highway north, about three hours, with a coffee stop on the way. Your first visit is the Catacombs of Kom el-Shoqafa, the largest Roman-era burial site in Egypt, cut into the rock in the 1st and 2nd centuries AD and found by chance in 1900 when a donkey fell through the ground. A spiral staircase leads down three levels to a banqueting hall and a main tomb chamber where the gods Anubis and Sobek appear dressed as Roman soldiers – a perfect picture of a city where Egyptian, Greek and Roman worlds blended.

Nearby stands Pompey's Pillar, a single column of red Aswan granite almost 27 metres high, raised around 297 AD in honour of the emperor Diocletian, on the hill of the Serapeum, the temple that once housed a daughter library of the famous Library of Alexandria. Sphinxes and underground galleries still surround it.

After a seafood lunch near the Eastern Harbour, where you choose your fish at the counter, you visit the Qaitbay Citadel, built by the Mamluk sultan Qaitbay around 1477 on the exact spot where the Pharos Lighthouse stood until earthquakes brought it down; some of its granite blocks were reused in the fort. From the walls you look back across the curve of the bay to the city. Next is the Bibliotheca Alexandrina, opened in 2002 as a tribute to the ancient Library, a tilted disc of glass and granite carved with letters from scripts of the whole world, with museums of antiquities and manuscripts inside. You finish with a drive along the Corniche before heading back to Cairo, arriving at about 19:30.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
07:00 – Pick-up from your hotel in Cairo or Giza.
10:00 – Catacombs of Kom el-Shoqafa (about 1 hour).
11:15 – Pompey's Pillar and the Serapeum (about 45 minutes).
12:30 – Seafood lunch by the Eastern Harbour.
14:00 – Qaitbay Citadel (about 1 hour).
15:15 – Bibliotheca Alexandrina (about 1 hour).
16:30 – Drive along the Corniche and return to Cairo.
19:30 – Arrival at your hotel.

GOOD TO KNOW
• The library is closed on some days of the week; we adjust the order or replace it with the Alexandria National Museum.
• Optional extras: the Roman Theatre at Kom el-Dikka or the Montaza Palace gardens.
• Alexandria is a lively modern city; traffic can change the timing.

INCLUDED: private vehicle and driver for the day, licensed Egyptologist guide, tickets to Kom el-Shoqafa, Pompey's Pillar, the Qaitbay Citadel and the Bibliotheca Alexandrina, seafood lunch, bottled water, pick-up and drop-off.
NOT INCLUDED: drinks at lunch, camera fees where charged, tips.

Overnight: none.
Meals: lunch.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose a date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only when the tour is confirmed.

faq.question: How long is the drive from Cairo?
faq.answer: About 3 hours each way on the desert highway, depending on traffic. The car is private and air-conditioned, and we stop for coffee on the way.

faq.question: Is Alexandria worth a day trip?
faq.answer: Yes, if you have three or more days in Cairo. It shows a completely different Egypt: Greek and Roman history, the Mediterranean and a relaxed seaside city.

faq.question: Can we see the remains of the Lighthouse or the ancient Library?
faq.answer: Neither survives above ground. The Qaitbay Citadel stands on the site of the Lighthouse, and the Serapeum hill by Pompey's Pillar held a branch of the Library. Your guide brings both stories to life.

faq.question: Is lunch included?
faq.answer: Yes, a seafood lunch near the harbour where you choose your fish. Meat and vegetarian options are available.

faq.question: Are the catacombs suitable for everyone?
faq.answer: They are reached by a spiral staircase and can be humid. People with limited mobility or claustrophobia may prefer to skip them; tell us and we will adjust.

faq.question: Is it suitable for children?
faq.answer: Yes. Children usually enjoy the citadel, the catacombs and the sea. The long drive is the main challenge.

faq.question: Can we go by train instead?
faq.answer: Yes. Trains run between Cairo and Alexandria in about 2.5 to 3 hours. We can meet you at Alexandria station with a car and guide.

faq.question: What if the library is closed?
faq.answer: If your date falls on a closing day, we replace it with the Alexandria National Museum or the Roman Theatre at Kom el-Dikka.

faq.question: Can we swim in the sea?
faq.answer: This is a sightseeing day without a beach stop, but in summer we can add time at a beach on request.

faq.question: What should I wear?
faq.answer: Comfortable shoes and light clothes, plus a jacket in winter, when the sea wind can be cool.

faq.question: Can we end the day in Alexandria?
faq.answer: Yes. You can stay overnight in Alexandria and continue your trip from there; tell us and we will adjust the transfer.

faq.question: What is the cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 24 hours before the tour. Until your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
